title: LDR Light Sensor Lab
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Light-Dependent Resistor
Voltage Divider
ADC
Photosensor
description: Interactive p5.js MicroSim of an LDR voltage divider: room brightness sets the LDR resistance, a fixed resistor slider changes the divider, and the schematic, worked formula and gauge show Vout and the 0-65535 ADC reading.

educational.topic: Reading an LDR with a voltage divider and the ADC
learningObjectives: Apply the voltage divider formula to calculate Vout for a given LDR resistance
Convert Vout into the 16-bit ADC reading that read_u16() returns
Explain how the choice of fixed resistor changes the sensor's useful range

keyQuestions: Why does brighter light give a bigger ADC reading with this wiring?
What happens to the reading if the LDR and fixed resistor swap places?
Which fixed resistor gives the most change between two light levels?
commonMisconceptions: The ADC measures resistance directly (it measures voltage)
Any fixed resistor works equally well (the best value is near the LDR resistance in the light range you care about)
assessmentOpportunities: Hand-calculate Vout and the ADC reading with answers hidden
Justify a fixed resistor value for an application

controls.label: Brightness
controls.range: Dark room to direct sunlight (LDR 1 Mohm to 500 ohm)

controls.label: Hide Vout and the ADC reading (predict first)
